title: Body mass slopes had opposite signs in six bird drought abundance samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested whether larger birds had less negative recorded abundance responses to drought within six studies in Australia, Hawaii, Spain and North Dakota. We used 173 records and 145 study-species units from a 2024 public release. Four slopes were negative and two were positive. All six corrected HC3 working-model intervals included zero. Diet adjustment kept all signs. In Hawaii, precision weights within species changed the slope from -0.107 to +0.054 source effect-size units per tenfold mass. The extract did not establish a common size advantage. Shared droughts and related species can violate the interval assumptions. Detection, publication bias, missing traits and incomplete dates limit inference. Balanced independent-period tests were not supported. No pollution effect or causal climate-change effect was tested. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Separate study slopes for log10 adult body mass. Lines are corrected HC3 working-model intervals. Diamonds are diet-adjusted slopes. Independent species errors are a necessary assumption for the interval interpretation.
